summary: Tai-shing Wut specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998) and served as an assistant professor at the City University of Hong Kong from 2009 to 2014.
Taido Kitamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Shuchiin University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and in another role attested from 1994 to 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. Educated at Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union, he studied under Reb Anderson and others. He has taught at Loyola University Chicago, Institute of Buddhist Studies, and several other institutions.

Taijun Inokuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University as a lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987), and served as representative for The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, later becoming a professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1912.
Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He held an assistant professor post at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2016. Mibu also served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Koyasan University and earned a PhD from Toyo University in 1994. He has held multiple posts at Koyasan University, including assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and professor.
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1933. Satomi served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1906) and Tokyo University of Education (~1906–1919).

Tairyo Makita (1912–2011) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto Universities. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1949–1976) and later as president of Saitama Institute of Technology in 1997.
Tairyu Tsunoda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a lecturer post at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and later served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), a professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Taisen Deshimaru (1914–1982) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kodo Sawaki from circa 1936 to 1965 and founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and earned a master's degree from the University of Tokyo, later serving as a professor at Komazawa University and a concurrent lecturer at the Eastern Institute (attested 1990).
Taishun Mibu (1913–1980) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University, graduating in 1937, and served as library director at Taisho University (attested 1972).

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, and held the Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion post at Smith College (1971–1998).
Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1948–1952) and under Mumon Yamada (~1954–1988). He later held a post at Hanazono University from circa 1996 to 2000.

Taixu (1890–1947) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang at Jinling Scriptural Press. He led the Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927) and founded several institutes, colleges, and Buddhist associations.
